Problem Statement in a line: The existing college printing setup depends on manually managing emails, printing done by people, and using handwritten logs, which leads to delays, inefficiency, and extra work for the staff.
Describe your problem statement in 200:
The current college printing system is pretty slow and relies on a manual process where students send their documents to a shared printer ID. Then, a staff member has to open each email, print the files, jot down details in a logbook, and collect payments. This whole setup results in long wait times, a heavy workload for staff, frequent mistakes, and a lack of transparency, especially during busy academic hours. There's no automated way to manage the queue, calculate costs, or keep digital records, which makes the system feel outdated and inefficient.
This project aims to tackle these problems by introducing an automated, self-service printing solution. It lets users upload their documents directly, takes care of the printing automatically, and creates digital logs for all print jobs. By getting rid of the email dependency and manual logging, this system cuts down on delays, boosts accuracy, and makes the entire printing process smoother while using the current infrastructure.

Problem Statement in a line: The absence of a centralized and dependable place for institution-specific academic resources results in scattered preparation and wasted time for students.

Problem Statement in a line: Increasing and Managing canteen queue efficienctly

The Smart Canteen Portal: Streamlining Campus Dining

To tackle persistent canteen crowding, we propose a digital portal that eliminates the two biggest bottlenecks: payment lines and waiting crowds.

The Workflow:
Through a dedicated interface, students can pre-plan their visit by booking a time slot and pre-ordering their meals. An integrated payment gateway handles transactions instantly, removing the need for cash or card queues at the counter. Once the order is placed, a digital token is sent to the canteen staff’s real-time dashboard.

Smart Notifications:
Instead of hovering near the kitchen, users are notified via the portal the moment their meal is ready. This "just-in-time" pickup system prevents physical congestion and allows students to stay productive until they are called.

The Impact:
By digitizing the workflow, the canteen shifts from a chaotic rush to a coordinated, high-efficiency service, saving time for students and staff alike.

Problem Statement in a line: To streamline campus canteen operations by reducing service delays and queues, improving food availability information, simplifying payments, and enabling structured student feedback and issue resolution through a smart digital platform.

The college canteen is a critical facility for students and hostellers at NFSU Tripura Campus, yet it currently faces multiple operational challenges that affect efficiency and user experience. One major issue is the delay in food preparation and service, particularly during peak hours, which leads to dissatisfaction among students. There is also no clear or centralized information regarding the daily menu, food availability, or preparation status, causing confusion and repeated inquiries at the canteen counter.
In addition, the manual ordering and payment process contributes to long physical queues, time wastage, and overcrowding. The lack of payment simplification and digital tracking makes transactions slower and harder to manage during busy periods. Another significant gap is the absence of a structured platform for student feedback, reviews, and issue reporting, which limits effective communication between students, canteen staff, and the concerned authorities. This also makes it difficult to identify and resolve recurring problems.

Overall, these issues—and other related operational and student-support challenges—arise due to manual processes and the lack of a centralized digital management system. There is a strong need for a smart, transparent, and efficient solution to streamline canteen operations, simplify payments, improve information flow, and enhance student satisfaction.

Problem Statement in a line: Absence of a centralized and organized Previous Year Question (PYQ) website for NFSU Tripura Campus students for semester-wise exam preparation
Describe your problem statement in 200:
Students at the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU), Tripura Campus often face difficulties when searching for Previous Year Question Papers (PYQs) for End Semester and Mid Semester examinations. At present, there is no single official website or platform where these question papers are available in an organized manner. Most students depend on WhatsApp groups, seniors, or personal collections, which are usually scattered, incomplete, or not properly arranged. This makes exam preparation stressful and time-consuming.

For junior students especially, the absence of a proper PYQ repository creates confusion about exam patterns, important topics, and the level of questions asked. Instead of focusing on learning, they spend a lot of time searching for study materials. Moreover, access to PYQs often depends on personal contacts, which means not every student gets equal opportunities.

Creating a centralized PYQ website for NFSU Tripura Campus can solve this problem effectively. The platform would provide semester-wise, subject-wise, and exam-wise question papers in one place. This will help students prepare better, understand expectations, and plan their studies more efficiently.

The proposed website aims to be simple, reliable, and student-friendly, allowing easy access to verified question papers and encouraging responsible sharing. This initiative will support juniors, reduce academic stress, and build a stronger learning culture on campus.
